title: Tokenizer hot-path: lightweight ASCII fast-path, session token cache, and prefill scheduling hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers with short ASCII prompts and high QPS observe disproportionately high prefill-side overhead (tokenization + normalization + routing). This ticket reduces per-request prefill latency and CPU cost by implementing a thin fast-path for common input shapes, a session-scoped token-id cache, and light-weight hints to kernel selection / prefill scheduler so requests are batched more effectively without increasing p99 latency. The work targets hosted and dedicated runtimes and must remain compatible with Private deployments.
technical_design: 1) ASCII fast-path: implement a single-pass UTF-8 scanner that handles ASCII-only inputs (common for English short prompts). This bypasses the full normalization regex and Unicode segmentation unless a non-ASCII byte is seen. 2) Session token cache: maintain an LRU token-id cache keyed by (session_id, token_string_prefix) to avoid reallocating token vectors for repeated prefixes (user sessions and templates often reuse initial phrases). 3) Background normalizer: offload expensive unicode-normalize/regex rules to a worker thread pool; pre-check on main thread for ASCII-only and short inputs. 4) Prefill scheduling hints: surface a small header from tokenizer with metadata (approx_tokens, is_ascii_only, common_prefix_hash) so prefill scheduler can group compatible requests and select kernel variant optimized for small sequences. 5) Kernel hint API: lightweight enumeration passed to runtime (SMALL_SEQ_FASTKERNEL | DEFAULT) to prefer kernels with lower startup overhead. 6) Metrics/tracing: instrument per-request path taken, cache hit/miss, normalizer fallback, and hint usage.
benchmarks: Baseline (canary): p50 6.2ms, p95 14.8ms, CPU 3.1 cores for 1000rps with 1-token prompts. Goal after landing: p50 <4ms, p95 <10ms for same workload and 20-30% CPU reduction. Microbench plan: run synthetic 1-3 token English prompts, mixed 30% non-ASCII to validate fallback, and production traffic replay for 24h. Collect tokenization_time_ms, total_prefill_ms, kernel_hint_effectiveness, cache_hit_rate.
acceptance_criteria:
- ASCII fast-path implemented and guarded by input inspection.
- Session token cache added; demonstrates >=30% cache hit rate in session-replay test.
- Prefill hint header emitted and consumed by scheduler on dedicated runtime.
- End-to-end benchmark shows p95 reduction >=20% and CPU reduction >=15% on synthetic short-prompt workload.
- No functional regressions: identical decoded tokens for fallback paths.
- Unit and integration tests covering ascii_only vs fallback, cache eviction, and hint propagation.
- Observability dashboards created: tokenization latency, cache hit %, hint routing breakdown.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the tokenizer fast-path + cache. 2) Canary on internal low-risk tenant for 48h with traffic shadowing. 3) Enable prefill hint consumption on a single runtime pool (dedicated region) and monitor kernel selection and latency. 4) Gradual rollout to 10% traffic, then 50%, then 100% pending no regressions. 5) For Private deployments, provide patch notes and opt-in flag; recommend schedule after 2 weeks of hosted stability.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: ASCII fast-path could diverge from full normalization for edge unicode inputs. Mitigation: exhaustive unit tests and a debug mode that compares outputs on a sample of requests and alerts on mismatch.
- Risk: Session cache memory blowup. Mitigation: LRU with strict per-session limits and global circuit-breaker; metrics to track memory pressure.
- Risk: Kernel hint misuse could reduce throughput for non-small sequences. Mitigation: conservative default (hint is advisory), scheduler experiments required with fallbacks to DEFAULT kernel.
- Risk: Increased complexity in observability. Mitigation: add structured tracing fields and sampling for detailed traces.
implementation_notes:
- Add Tokenizer::fast_scan_utf8() that returns (is_ascii_only, approx_tokens, common_prefix_hash) quickly.
- Implement SessionTokenCache as an in-process LRU keyed by session_id with TTL. Start with capacity 512 entries per session.
- Expose hint header X-Runtime-Tokenizer-Hint in internal protocol used between gateway and runtime. Use compact encoding.
- Update runtime kernel selector to accept hint enum and prefer LOW_STARTUP kernels when SMALL_SEQ_FASTKERNEL is set.
- Create unit tests in tokenization_test.cpp and end-to-end in runtime_perf_integration.test.
- Add feature flag runtime.tokenizer_fastpath.enabled and runtime.tokenizer_prefill_hint.enabled.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed — ascii-only scanner prototype reduces CPU in microbench by 42%. 2026-02-20: Session cache RFC reviewed by Marco and Priya; concerns about memory bounds addressed. 2026-02-24: Implemented fast_scan_utf8 and integrated hint header emission; internal API review pending. 2026-02-28: End-to-end shadowing started on staging; initial cache hit_rate 36% for replay dataset.
